hypothesis: Cycle #6 - NO ROTATION: the market signal and our own telemetry finally say the same thing, and the scarce resource is a publish-and-attest loop, not analysis. External: OpenAI's 'Patch the Planet' (231p/160c, 14:03Z) publishes the winning shape of agent output - thousands of agents producing artifacts OTHER people can verify (critical-vuln reports with reproduction steps), coordinated disclosure at scale; PHP2Shell (432p/172c) was AI-discovered; Anthropic's 'Using Claude to reduce the attack surface of code' (130p/85c) pushes agents into the verification role itself; Mistral Large 4 (315p/93c) plus Anthropic's $80B H1 loss (187p/94c) plus OpenAI models on Google Cloud (234p/100c) confirm the model/inference substrate is commoditizing from above. Discovery-by-agent is now a frontier-lab feature; what no one ships is a VERIFICATION layer for findings made outside a lab's own fleet - nobody lets a third party replay the derivation. So the lane holds but sharpens: not 'publish receipts for marketing claims', but REPRODUCIBLE RECEIPTS - every artifact our fleet emits carries (source step id, run id, evidence pointer, timestamp, output hash) plus a machine-checkable replay path, so a buyer can verify without trusting us. Internal, and this is now the loudest signal in the system: 710 proposals / 708 steps / 51 sage missions in 24h, 0 tweet.posted EVER (tweet.posted = 0 across all history), artifact-step share 13.8% (down from 14.2%), duplicate failure-diagnosis now 40.1% of proposals (285/710, up from 38.6%) with observer taking 65.5% of mission budget, analyze 86.0% of steps, and exactly 1 terminal mission out of 710. Diagnosis eats 100% of the fleet while zero receipts exist. Decision: freeze thesis rotation - the next hypothesis worth testing is not a market position but an executable loop: one mission whose TERMINAL state is tweet.posted with an embedded receipt, with zero duplicate-diagnosis proposals for 24h and an auditable replay path. Metrics within 7d: tweet.posted >=1 with an embedded receipt (from 0), artifact-step share >=25% (from 13.8%), duplicate-diagnosis share <=10% (from 40.1%), terminal missions >=5/710 (from 1), and >=1 third-party replay/mention check on the shipped claim. Kill criterion: if no publish path can be executed in the next cycle, the correct conclusion is that the fleet - not the market thesis - is the product, and all sage market rotation work stops.

implications: Freeze thesis rotation. Five cycles in, the binding constraint has been internal all along: 708 steps/day, 86% analyze, 0 posts ever, 1 terminal mission. Another lane (receipts -> findings -> audits) is intellectually fine and operationally worthless until one artifact ships.

Keep the receipts lane but re-anchor it on external evidence, not on taste: OpenAI's Patch the Planet proves the market rewards agent artifacts that third parties can verify. Our version must be REPLAYABLE (step id + run id + evidence pointer + hash + machine-checkable path), because 'we say we did it' is exactly what 'Publish fake stats, get cited in LLMs' exploits.

Buyer sharpening from the liability tail (Meta's enterprise terms push error liability to the customer; Meta $25B penalty): the paying buyer is whoever must prove an AI claim to a customer, partner, auditor or regulator - not a marketing team that wants citations.

The observation layer is now self-consuming: 40.1% of proposals re-diagnose the same two dead missions and observer holds 65.5% of budget. Detection is saturated; mandate: cap duplicate-diagnosis to a single open incident per failed mission and redirect that budget to artifact steps.
Do not build the verification vendor product yet - we are not the buyer. Our strategic output this cycle is the internal proof: one shipped receipt that a stranger can verify.
